blocks.heading: Brand name, loyalty and image
blocks.text: A brand name identifies an offering and distinguishes it from competitors. Brand loyalty is repeated preference and purchasing of that brand. Brand image is the identity or impression associated with it. A business can choose a name and communicate an intended image, but customers’ actual experiences influence the image they hold. Recognition is not itself loyalty: someone may know the name and still buy a rival. A strong image can support differentiation, but it needs credible quality and service rather than unsupported claims.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Oru Gear names its bag “Tana”. Buyers associate it with durability and some repeatedly choose it. Tana is the name; the durability association is image; repeated choice is loyalty. They are connected but not definitions of the same thing.

blocks.heading: Brand name
blocks.text: A brand name is the unique name of a product that distinguishes it from other brands. It helps recognition and can support repeat identification, but a name alone does not establish quality, loyalty or a particular customer image. Consistent use and a reliable experience can help the name become meaningful.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A tool bag is named “Oru Carry”. Oru Carry is the identifying name; whether buyers associate it with strength and repeatedly choose it concerns image and loyalty respectively.

blocks.heading: Brand loyalty
blocks.text: Brand loyalty is when customers keep buying the same brand again and again instead of choosing a competitor’s brand. It can support repeat demand and reduce switching, but depends on customer experience and alternatives. Awareness or one trial purchase is not enough to establish loyalty.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A buyer repeatedly chooses Omi Bags after satisfactory use despite available alternatives. That repeated preference illustrates loyalty. Merely recognising the logo would not show the same behaviour.

blocks.heading: Brand image
blocks.text: Brand image is the identity or impression associated with an offering, distinguishing it from rivals. It can concern reliability, affordability, design or other perceived qualities. The business can communicate an intended identity, while customers’ experience influences the image actually held. It differs from the identifying name and the behaviour of repeat buying.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Customers describe Hela Cases as practical and durable. That association describes image. The product name identifies it; repeated purchases would be evidence of loyalty.
